description: Annotated good and bad examples from the iamar build. Each entry is a real outcome that the source document records: WORKS, PARTIAL or FAILED. Pictures stay in the source repository; this file cites where each one lives (source). Rebuild gallery.md with gallery.py build.

entries.title: Every landmark cut its door at the house height
entries.seen: Landmarks shared the house door height, so the big buildings lost their grandeur.
entries.lesson: Give each landmark its own entrance height in its spec; carry the scale with the arch ring and painted carving, not extra polygons.

entries.title: Monumental gate and bridges: grandeur from width and rhythm
entries.seen: A 6.1 m bridge against a 14 m street narrowed the grandest moment of the route.
entries.lesson: Set gate and bridge widths from the approach, not from the minimum road. The South target of 18-20 m stayed open at the time of writing.

entries.title: Street lamps placed inside the carriageway
entries.seen: On a 3 m castle road the lamps sat 0.35 m inside the paved edge.
entries.lesson: Offset lamps outside the road half-width plus a margin (w * 0.5 + 0.6 m) and test them against the road ribbon.

entries.title: Extra LOD levels on baked building shells
entries.seen: Levels past the 1 m error cap lost windows, trims and lit windows at 50-110 m. Three audit rounds over 76 views gained 0.86% of primitives.
entries.lesson: Do not add simplifier levels to baked shells for a small gain. Lossless savings need per-building impostors or a far-LOD set.

entries.title: Coarsest baked LOD cut on 148 of 197 meshes
entries.seen: The round cut 37.1% of triangles at the coarsest level (361,706 to 227,541). Windows and lit windows failed at 50-110 m and nothing was published.
entries.lesson: Judge a LOD round by what is visible at its switch distance, in a rendered view, before counting triangles.

entries.title: Hidden-face culling on buildings
entries.seen: Removing the hidden faces of buildings saved 0.8% of LOD0 triangles, because the generator already culled them. A dressing split netted -0.8% to +0.2% with 11 more draw calls.
entries.lesson: Measure a culling pass on the real building set before adding it. Long dressing pieces must stay readable at range.

entries.title: Instance uniforms for per-house looks
entries.seen: A shared instance-uniform buffer overflowed at 4,096 items.
entries.lesson: Use material variants for per-house looks; do not rely on instance uniform buffers for large sets.

entries.title: Night far trees glow white
entries.seen: Impostor billboards at night were not lit like real trees and glowed white.
entries.lesson: Fixed on 2026-10-09; the root cause was the same as the normal-atlas encoding trap. Check far impostors in night light.

entries.title: Far-only tree impostor cards
entries.seen: On the Balanced preset, far-only tree cards dropped the frame rate from 42 to 24 fps.
entries.lesson: Measure impostor cards on the target preset. Cutting at 50-60 m with better blended cards is the open proposal.

entries.title: Forest LOD: blocky canopy and snapping impostors
entries.seen: Blocky crowns and 22.5-degree view snapping made trees look as if they changed shape.
entries.lesson: Keep the crown silhouette across LODs and avoid snapping impostor views on a coarse angle grid.

entries.title: Raising the mesh LOD threshold under load
entries.seen: Raising the threshold above 4 px visibly broke a fountain about 15 m away and simplified stalls at x8.
entries.lesson: Under load, reduce render scale first; use mesh LOD only at the floor.

entries.title: LOD flag on painted ground
entries.seen: generate_lods on ground with class colours and UV seams cut the slice by 1.8%. Position-only far siblings halved the paved meshes but the net gain was about 1% of a view.
entries.lesson: Do not expect the LOD flag to help painted ground. Build a far re-gridded tile.

entries.title: Derivative bump on small creatures
entries.seen: bump * texture scale made a crosshatch on small creatures. Bump at 0 read as smooth feathers.
entries.lesson: Keep bump low on small creatures; test it at the viewing distance.

entries.title: Griffin beak covered the face like a mask
entries.seen: The beak grew from the skull end ring and read as a big yellow toucan beak.
entries.lesson: Grow the beak from the feathered face, compressed to about 0.74x with a dark tip.

entries.title: Lowering horse detail to the budget
entries.seen: LOD0 went from 9,780 to 8,284 triangles against a 6k budget. Lower detail lost the hooves and the loft profile between stations.
entries.lesson: Keep hooves and the loft profile when cutting; meet the budget with texture and bake instead of cutting silhouette.

entries.title: Rebuilt MultiMesh lost the instance colour
entries.seen: A creature script rebuilt the body MultiMesh and read the coat tint back too early. The body drew black while head and legs kept colour.
entries.lesson: Each instance restores its coat on its first pose. Verify instance colours in the game, not in a headless run.

entries.title: Procedural legs float on uneven ground
entries.seen: Separate lower-leg parts with knee and hock flex are not IK. Blender inspection caught floating wolf paws.
entries.lesson: Overlap the pastern and paw so no gap shows, and inspect feet in Blender at the walking pose.

entries.title: Beard stretched over the collar by the hair fit
entries.seen: A posed fit loop over every hair mesh, beards included, pushed the beard tip out over a chain collar. The run failed at score 87.4 from 90.4.
entries.lesson: Skip beards in the posed fit; they follow the build through body weights.

entries.title: Herd close and far mesh switch
entries.seen: A cow went from 7,604 close triangles to 21,924 with the close mesh; the far mesh is 2,418.
entries.lesson: Switch at 22 m and back within 18 m using the closest member. The swap is discrete with no crossfade, and close detail multiplies the cost, so set a budget first.

entries.title: Multi-view generation traps on a winged creature
entries.seen: Front-only views gave blob backs. Side views folded the wings into the cloak. A thin sword vanished. Flat grey patches became planks.
entries.lesson: Name the wings in the prompt with a negative prompt, pick from several seeds, and drop flat untextured patches before modelling.

entries.title: Paving disc 3 cm under the lowest ground point
entries.seen: The paving disc z-fought with the ground wherever the ground dipped below it.
entries.lesson: Cut the footprint out of the ground and lay paving 2-5 cm above it with a kerb ring. Check fountains, wells, statues and stalls.

entries.title: Far ground groups show coarse flat ground through fine paving
entries.seen: Far ground groups were measured from the group centre, so coarse ground showed through fine paving near the player.
entries.lesson: Measure far-LOD visibility range from the player, not from the group centre.

entries.title: Footing faces below ground bake black
entries.seen: Footing tops at street level baked black and showed as strips where the ground dipped. Rebaking did not help until the geometry was culled or sunk.
entries.lesson: Cull or sink hidden footing faces before baking; a rebake alone will not fix them.

entries.title: Pond water floating above the terrain
entries.seen: Water was raised 0.25 m over a 1.42x shoreline, and the height shelf ran after the terrain hook.
entries.lesson: Dip the basin below ground and slope the banks. Apply the height shelf before the terrain hook.

entries.title: Dry pale apron round a pond reads as a sand smear
entries.seen: The carve flattened an apron 0.2 m above the water. It read as a dry sand smear.
entries.lesson: Raise the water over the apron or dip the bowl; keep shafts and haze 8 m off the water.

entries.title: Road ribbon built before the pond was carved
entries.seen: The road ribbon lay across the water and the bridge deck.
entries.lesson: Defer the road build until the ground is carved, skip rows over the pond and the bridge decks, and keep waymarkers off the bridge.

entries.title: Warm peach fog tinted the valley yellow
entries.seen: Warm fog tinted the whole valley yellow when seen from the air.
entries.lesson: Keep the warmth in the sun and the surfaces; keep the fog cool and light.

entries.title: Lighting a focal statue
entries.seen: Warm key from braziers, a cool rim, shafts and animated flame cards read well. A flickering light moved the shadows.
entries.lesson: Use real animated flames with embers so the light and the shadows move together.

entries.title: Reduced lightmap decoded to the wrong format
entries.seen: An LA8 lightmap decoded as RGBA8 lost the sun shadows and washed out the walls.
entries.lesson: Convert decoded images back to the stored format, and test that the sun is read from alpha.

entries.title: Shadow cost measured with the wrong sun
entries.seen: The budget tool used 4 splits over 60 m, so a 25k-triangle landmark drew as 101k shadow triangles. The shipped game uses 1 split over 45 m; the true share was 16-24% of the frame, not 41-49%.
entries.lesson: Measure with the shipped lighting, not a tool default.

entries.title: Blob shadow reads as a black hole
entries.seen: On the Fast preset the sun shadows were off, and an unshaded near-black disc drew under characters. Five players reported it as a black spot.
entries.lesson: Use alpha around 0.25, tint it to the ground, multiply-blend it and fade it at night and in rain.

entries.title: Covered passages bake near-black
entries.seen: Road decks inside gate passages baked at sky 0.08 with no sun and read 10-12% of open-road brightness.
entries.lesson: Hold sky light at 0.6 on up-facing texels of named fortification meshes, or add lamps.

entries.title: LOD swaps judged on stills
entries.seen: Far-level switches and hand-overs show as horizon rings and pops that stills do not reveal.
entries.lesson: Judge LOD swaps on 30 fps frame sequences. A hard switch may need a 1-2 m hysteresis band.

entries.title: Hero face pasted onto image-to-3D statues
entries.seen: Sculpts decimated to 3,500-8,000 triangles gave soft blob faces. A pasted hero face (about 10,032 triangles in total) was called horrible and removed in an internal task.
entries.lesson: Do not paste a hero face mesh onto a generated statue. Fix the sculpt at its source.

entries.title: Statues from posed character models
entries.seen: A CPU-skinned posed mesh of about 2k triangles with AO in vertex colour worked. The moat-bridge statue drew black and stays open.
entries.lesson: Check the bake and the UV2 and material of every statue after a worker-thread load.

entries.title: Stale bake signature draws a statue unbaked
entries.seen: A reverted mesh no longer matched its bake, so the game drew it with live light and no baked AO.
entries.lesson: Compare before and after shots only after the bake signature matches the built mesh.

entries.title: Imported split normals stopped Godot making LODs
entries.seen: The first bake exported 23,970 split vertices. Godot generated no LODs for the custom split normals.
entries.lesson: Clear custom split normals before export, or Godot silently makes no LODs.

entries.title: Harness reported PASS despite script errors
entries.seen: A pond fixture reported PASS while its dependencies logged SCRIPT ERRORs.
entries.lesson: A green run is not proof. Fail the run on any script error in the log, and check the log, not only the exit code.

entries.title: Stale class cache gave RESULT ok with parse errors
entries.seen: A stale global script class cache printed RESULT ok while the scripts had parse errors.
entries.lesson: Clear the class cache before a gate run; treat parse errors as a failure.

entries.title: Probe exited 0 while a check had failed
entries.seen: The probe printed exit 0 while script errors hid a failed check.
entries.lesson: Make the probe count errors and exit non-zero on any failed check.
